Reframed with the SLOOS (July 2021) lens: The Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey indicates a broadly improving credit backdrop that reinforces the FOMC’s accommodative stance. Banks reported easing terms for C&I loans and stronger loan demand across large, middle‑market, and small firms, alongside higher borrower inquiries. Foreign banks also reported stronger C&I demand tied to inventories, accounts receivable, capex, and M&A. On the household side, banks eased standards for consumer credit (credit cards, auto, other), and residential mortgage lending generally saw easing in several categories (with GSE-eligible standards largely unchanged, stronger demand for qualified mortgages, and few subprime originations). Multifamily CRE standards also eased. Taken together, SLOOS suggests credit supply and demand are aligned to support growth and employment, tempering some of the caution from the FSR (elevated valuations, nonbank vulnerabilities) and virus risks. Net tone: positive and more constructive than the FSR-only read.
